exposure: Mode of delivery (planned C-section, unplanned C-section, vaginal delivery)
cohort: 570 mother-child pairs from the WHEALS birth cohort in Detroit, Michigan
finding: Children born via planned cesarean section had a higher risk of preadolescent obesity compared to those born vaginally, while there was no significant association between unplanned C-section and obesity.
mod_finding: Children born via planned C-section had 1.77 times higher risk of obesity (≥95th percentile) compared to vaginal deliveries.
birth_weight: Mentioned but specific values not provided
